fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Closely-spaced intersection queuing/turning/parking conflicts on a corridor with recorded high-accident designation is a genuine preliminary-design-stage safety issue with clear crash-producing mechanisms.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal conflict-mechanism claim is backed by a verbatim quote from EV-US-016 matching the statement text, and the high-accident corridor detail is presented as recorded scheme fact.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA preliminary-design semantics, with no compliance question conflated into the safety issue.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommends two concrete, viable preliminary-design measures—turning-movement restrictions and relocating specified parking stalls outside the intersection functional area—rather than a null action.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as potentially present on the commercial corridor, but their exposure to parking/turning maneuvers near the intersection is not analyzed, consistent with a scoped-out-but-acknowledged treatment.

justifications.substance: Queue spillback between signals 650 ft apart causing upstream intersection blockage is a recognized, scheme-specific safety issue squarely addressable at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal 650-ft spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quote (EV-US-001); spillback is explicitly labeled as derived inference and confidence traces to the recorded case-study table rather than invention.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern with no normative basis asserted, keeping the safety question distinct from any compliance determination under FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Signal coordination plus Do Not Block Intersection signing and conspicuousness upgrades are specific, standard, and viable at preliminary design, though queue-storage verification criteria could sharpen it further.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists at both signalized crossings are explicitly identified and the scoping to vehicle occupants is reasoned, satisfying consideration of VRU relevance for this mechanism.
